items.stem: To cut picker travel time in a warehouse, how should fast-moving (A-class) SKUs generally be slotted?

options.text: Close to dispatch and in easy-reach 'golden zone' locations
options.rationale: Correct: placing high-velocity items near shipping and at ergonomic heights minimises travel and strain.

options.text: In the furthest aisles to keep dispatch clear
options.rationale: Distant slotting increases travel for the most-picked items.

options.text: Spread evenly so no aisle is busy
options.rationale: Even spreading ignores velocity and raises average travel for popular SKUs.

options.text: On the top racking levels to save floor space
options.rationale: Top levels slow picking and add safety risk for high-velocity items.

items.explanation: Correct: placing high-velocity items near shipping and at ergonomic heights minimises travel and strain.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are advantages of ABC cycle counting over a single annual physical inventory? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It finds and fixes errors continuously through the year
options.rationale: Correct: frequent counting surfaces process causes early rather than once a year.

options.text: It counts high-value or fast-moving items more often
options.rationale: Correct: ABC focuses effort where inaccuracy costs the most.

options.text: It removes the need to investigate discrepancies
options.rationale: Discrepancies still need root-cause investigation; counting only detects them.

options.text: It guarantees 100% accuracy at all times
options.rationale: No counting method guarantees perfect accuracy; it manages and improves it.

items.explanation: Correct: frequent counting surfaces process causes early rather than once a year.

items.stem: A warehouse has many orders that each contain the same few SKUs during a promotion. Which picking method is usually most efficient?

options.rationale: Correct: batching groups many orders for the same SKUs into one pick trip, cutting travel.
Picking one order at a time repeats travel for the same SKUs.
Zoning alone still walks each order separately within the zone.
Unstructured picking raises travel and error, especially at volume.

items.explanation: Correct: batching groups many orders for the same SKUs into one pick trip, cutting travel.
